confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'very strong evidence' and 'effectively the expected diagnosis' are reasonably hedged after the open-circuit test

compatibilityWithoutEvidence.evidence: Says the exact pump version must be matched using E-Nr/FD, so no unsupported fit claim

rationale: The assistant correctly identified E:09 as a heating fault, offered the isolated resistance test with sensible safety steps, and after the customer reported an open circuit it pointed to heat pump assembly replacement. It gave a balanced repair-vs-replace view and advised an engineer if the customer isn't confident, and it said the part must be matched by E-Nr. Minor weaknesses: it quoted costs and resistance figures with some confidence, and it overstated that sensor or wiring faults are unlikely, since the open-circuit heater reading only confirms the heater itself and does not exclude other faults. It also told the customer to switch off at the socket and turn off the water, but it did not stress strongly enough that the test should be done unplugged and with the connector removed.</br>
